title: Intermittent affinity-fragmentation batch-drain freeze causing long-tail latency
creator: Priya Shah
description: Summary: On 2025-02-08 and again on 2025-02-09 we observed reproducible multi-minute tail latency spikes for a subset of tenant traffic served by the continuous batching runtime. Symptoms were a small fraction (~0.6%) of requests experiencing 10x-50x token latency while the majority remained within SLO. The batches for affected requests appeared to stop draining even though GPU utilization remained nominal. This ticket documents the incident, root-cause analysis, mitigations applied, and concrete follow-ups to prevent recurrence.

2025-02-08 03:22 UTC - Triage: narrow to continuous-batching shard us-west-2-a. Observed cohort of requests with 'affinity_id' skew.
2025-02-08 03:35 UTC - Mitigation: temporarily disabled affinity-based packing for affected shard; latency returned to baseline within 2 minutes.
2025-02-09 11:05 UTC - Regression recur: similar pattern after an autoscaler adjustment during a traffic ramp. Triggered full incident review.
2025-02-09 11:40 UTC - Root-cause hypothesis formed: affinity hash fragmentation leading to long-lived opaque queue nodes that prevented timely batch drain under certain slot reclamation heuristics.
2025-02-09 12:10 UTC - Rollforward mitigation: introduce conservative slot reclamation backoff and eviction for idle affinity groups. Applied as hotfix; monitoring enabled.
2025-02-09 13:00 UTC - Incident declared mitigated. Post-incident collection of traces, heap profiles, and batch coordinator diagnostics.
2025-02-11 09:00 UTC - Deeper RCA: found interaction between per-tenant affinity packing and preemption during autoscaler shrink that left fragmented batch descriptors referencing stale queue heads.
2025-02-12 15:30 UTC - Engineering review: scheduled rollout of robust affinity-compact operation and added invariants to prevent stale head pointers.
2025-02-17 10:00 UTC - PR opened for unit/integration tests and telemetry: GH PR #6129 - batching: affinity compaction and head-sanity checks.
2025-02-18 16:45 UTC - RFC draft for long-term policy: adaptive affinity reshuffle vs. deterministic hashing to balance fairness and throughput.
2025-02-18 17:15 UTC - Ticket moved to In Review pending design sign-off and stakeholder approvals.
root_cause_summary: A corner-case interaction between affinity-based request packing and node reclamation during autoscaler events produced fragmented queue structures with stale head pointers. Those fragments were treated as live affinity groups by the batch coordinator, preventing batch formation for new requests associated with the same affinity buckets until explicit eviction. The bug was triggered when an autoscaler shrink interleaved with affinity-affecting reconnects; kernel-level scheduling and KV-cache usage were not the primary contributors.
mitigations_applied: Hotfix: disabled affinity-based packing for affected shard (fast rollback path).
Backoff: conservative slot-reclamation backoff to avoid preemption races during autoscaler shrink.
Eviction: introduced idle-affinity eviction after configurable grace period.
Monitoring: added affinity-group depth and head-age telemetry to Canary dashboards.
Alerting: new alerts for 'affinity_head_age > 60s' and 'affinity_eviction_rate == 0 while affinity_group_count > baseline'.
action_items: ENG-84567-1: Implement affinity compaction routine that runs during low load to coalesce fragmented groups (owner: Luca Martinez, due: 2025-03-07).
ENG-84567-2: Add deterministic invariants and unit tests to prevent stale-head references in the batch coordinator (owner: Aisha Raman, due: 2025-02-24).
ENG-84567-3: Instrument per-tenant affinity skew metrics and add a per-tenant fairness dashboard in Console (owner: Marta Kowalski, due: 2025-03-01).
ENG-84567-4: Run a cross-shard chaos exercise that simulates autoscaler shrink/reconnect interleavings and validate eviction/compaction (owner: Evan Brooks, due: 2025-03-10).
ENG-84567-5: Post-deploy runbook update: include steps to detect and remediate affinity-fragmentation (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2025-02-21).
ENG-84567-6: Evaluate long-term change: move from strict affinity packing to adaptive reshuffle policy and draft cost/latency tradeoff RFC (owner: Carlos D'Souza, due: 2025-03-21).
resolution_summary: Short-term mitigations (disable affinity packing on affected shards, conservative slot reclamation, and idle eviction) restored SLOs. Root cause fixed in codepath and covered by new unit/integration tests. Longer-term work includes compaction, telemetry, and a policy RFC to avoid similar regressions when autoscaler events interact with affinity heuristics.
